body: Just tried to avoid process.env in middleware and it seems that the process.env variables are not available in the whole application. Not only middlewares

Still an issue in released version v13.4.13 AFAICT

And not specific to docker, but any source of environment variables.
Seems to be related / same as https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/53579

issue.title: env empty when using zod validation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: Output
labels.description: Related to the the output configuration option.

issue.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: x64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.5.0: Thu Jun  8 22:22:22 PDT 2023; root:xnu-8796.121.3~7/RELEASE_X86_64
    Binaries:
      Node: 18.12.1
      npm: 8.19.2
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: 8.6.11
    Relevant Packages:
      next: 13.4.14-canary.1
      eslint-config-next: 13.4.13
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
      typescript: 5.1.6
    Next.js Config:
      output: standalone
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

App Router, Standalone mode (output: "standalone")

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug

https://github.com/JipSterk/next-app-dir-no-env

### To Reproduce

- clone the repo
- install dependencies with pnpm i
- cp .env.example .env
- update .env with GITHUB_ID & GITHUB_SECRET from https://github.com/settings/apps
  - the homepage should be http://localhost:3000
  - the callback url should be http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/github
- run docker compose up
- go to localhost:3000 an error should occur stating that zod couldn't validate any of the variables as they are undefined?

### Describe the Bug

the env variables should be validated as being defined. 
a `console.log(process.env)` confirms that the variables are there but still the zod schema cannot validate them.
i've tried importing `require('dotenv/config')` in `next.config.js` but this doesn't help.
it might have something to do with rcs and handling variables prefixed with: NEXT_PUBLIC_ but that's just a guess

### Expected Behavior

no zod validation error and all the env variables being defined in both rsc and client components

### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

Chromium Engine Version 115.0.5790.170

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

_No response_

issue.title: Environment variable behavior changed on 13.4.13-canary

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: Output
labels.description: Related to the the output configuration option.

issue.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.5.0: Thu Jun  8 22:22:20 PDT 2023; root:xnu-8796.121.3~7/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.18.0
      npm: 8.19.2
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: N/A
    Relevant Packages:
      next: 13.4.13-canary.14
      eslint-config-next: 13.4.12
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
      typescript: 5.1.6
    Next.js Config:
      output: standalone
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

Standalone mode (output: "standalone")

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug

https://github.com/asmockler/next-bug-runtime-env-vars

### To Reproduce

Create a standalone app and try to access an environment variable set not-at-build-time.

`console.log(process.env.TEST)` will evaluate to `undefined` for both of the following commands:

```
node .next/standalone/server.js
TEST=present node .next/standalone/server.js
```

I would expect the first to be `undefined` and the second to be `present`

### Describe the Bug

Environment variables are not accessible when set after build-time.

### Expected Behavior

Environment variables should be accessible and able to be overridden at runtime.

### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

Server-side

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

Standalone w/ Docker on Google Cloud Run

body: Any timeline when it will be fixed and released? This bug broke my production. 😑
@DominicWrege by chance have you tried with latest release ?

> @DominicWrege by chance have you tried with latest release ?

Still reproducible as of `13.4.16-canary.1`.

Yup. Well, currently there doesn't seem to be any workaround other than pinning it to 13.4.12.

https://github.com/florianliebig/nextjs-error-docker-13.4.13
The PoC he created also does not output console logs with the current Canary.

@belgattitude Yes it is still broken for me in `13.4.13, 13.4.14, 13.4.15` and `13.4.16`  😥

@k725 this works but should not be a go-to workaround.

Did runtime `process.env` access get deprecated alongside the `getConfig` API?

I wonder what is supposed to be the "correct" way of doing runtime configuration for Next.js these days, if neither of these are tested or supported 🤔
